settings.heading: True soap, foaming dispenser, no detergents.

settings.text: Soap works by surrounding oil and dirt with soap molecules so water can rinse them away — no sulfate detergents required. The foaming dispenser stretches a small amount of true coconut soap into a full lather, so your hands aren't hit with concentrated surfactant on every wash.

settings.title: Saponified Organic Virgin Coconut Oil
settings.text: The base. Cold-pressed virgin coconut oil reacted with potassium hydroxide produces soap molecules and naturally occurring glycerin — the entire cleansing system, with no added surfactants. Coconut-based soap is naturally high in lauric and capric acid soap chains, which lather well and lift oil and dirt without stripping the skin's lipid layer the way SLS does.

settings.title: Built for the Foaming Dispenser
settings.text: Diluted, not weakened. The same coconut-oil saponification as the bar — diluted to foaming-pump consistency and designed for the foaming dispenser, not a standard pump. The pump aerates a small amount into a generous lather, which means less product per wash than conventional pump soap. A regular pump will dispense it as a runny liquid and waste most of it.

settings.title: Variation Essential Oils
settings.text: Scent without synthetic fragrance. Each variation has a different blend of organic essential oils, named individually on the back panel — never a "fragrance" umbrella hiding undisclosed compounds. Orange Zest is orange, bergamot, spearmint, lemon, and grapefruit oils. Coconut Breeze is organic coconut oil extract. Calming Lavender is lavender oil. Pure Unscented has no oils added — just the natural light scent of saponified coconut oil.

settings.heading: Why does this only work in a foaming dispenser?
settings.row_content: The formula is intentionally thinner than conventional pump soap because the foaming dispenser does the work — it aerates a small amount of liquid into a full lather on contact. A standard pump will dispense it as a runny liquid and waste most of it down the drain. If you're refilling from the 32oz, use a foaming pump bottle, not a regular one.

settings.heading: What's actually in this soap?
settings.row_content: Saponified organic virgin coconut oil, water, and — depending on the variation — named organic essential oils. That's it. Saponification is the chemical reaction between coconut oil and potassium hydroxide that produces soap molecules and naturally occurring glycerin. The lye fully reacts during the process; no free alkali remains in the finished soap.

settings.heading: Why doesn't it foam as densely as my old hand soap?
settings.row_content: Conventional foaming soaps use cocamidopropyl betaine and SLS as secondary surfactants to build a thick, stable foam. We don't include either. The foam you get here is true coconut soap aerated by the dispenser — generous and lifting, but lighter than detergent foam. Foam isn't cleaning; the soap molecules are. Your hands are getting just as clean.

settings.heading: Is this safe for kids and sensitive hands?
settings.row_content: We formulated it for exactly that customer. No SLS, no synthetic fragrance, no propylene glycol, no dyes — the most common triggers in pump soap. The Pure Unscented variation is the most conservative choice for reactive skin. Many families with frequently washed kid hands tell us their cracked-knuckle problem eased after switching off detergent-based soaps.

settings.heading: Why does the Unscented version smell faintly like coconut?
settings.row_content: That's the soap itself, not added fragrance. Cold-pressed virgin coconut oil keeps a natural scent through saponification — refined oil wouldn't, because the deodorizing process strips it out along with the lauric acid. The scent is light and fades on the rinse. If you want truly zero scent, no soap made from real virgin oil will give you that.

settings.heading: How is this different from 'natural' foaming soaps at the grocery store?
settings.row_content: Read the back panel. Many soaps marketed as natural still contain sodium lauryl sulfate, cocamidopropyl betaine, propylene glycol, parabens, or synthetic fragrance under the umbrella term "parfum." The word natural isn't regulated in personal-care labeling. Our differentiation isn't natural-vs-conventional — it's a specific, short ingredient list you can read against any alternative on the shelf.

settings.heading: How do I refill from the 32oz?
settings.row_content: The 32oz is the same concentration as the bottle — pour directly into your foaming pump dispenser, no dilution needed. If you've used the soap before, rinse residue from the pump mechanism so it doesn't clog. Shake gently before use if the bottle has been sitting; coconut-based soap can settle slightly without separating.
